sheet-1.description: The lower half of the title sheet of the 1924 Elmer atlas, below the heavy line that separates it from the key map, index and title block. It shows the north-east corner of the business district: the east side of North Main Street from East Front Street down past State Street to Mill Street, and the open ground east of it as far as the shore of Lake Elmer. East Front Street runs along the top, with a few dwellings and outbuildings on its south side numbered 26 to 56; State Street is lettered where it meets North Main Street from the west. The Pennsylvania Railroad's West Jersey and Seashore line crosses the sheet diagonally from East Front Street to North Main Street near State Street, with a siding curving off to the east. Along North Main Street stand stores, a wall paper shop, a concrete-block store and dwellings, and behind them a garage for 30 cars with a show room, a grain and feed warehouse beside the railroad, and a large livery stable. South of the railroad are an auto repair shop, a blacksmith shop and storage buildings on the north side of Mill Street. The south-east part of the sheet is taken up by the A. Bolnick saw and grist mill (capacity 20 tons per day, steam power), sheds, ice houses on the shore and the open water of Lake Elmer. Streets are lettered 40 to 58 ft wide, and water pipes of four to eight inches are shown. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; the area south of the mill is marked no exposure.
notes: The upper half of the sheet (key map at 800 ft to an inch, index, water facilities and fire department notes) is masked out.
East Front is today's Front Street; the abandoned railroad corridor east of North Main Street is now followed by Harding Highway (US 40).
A. Bolnick saw and grist mill on the lake shore.

Map (50 ft). Upper half is the key map (800 ft), index and title block, masked out; lower half shows N. Main, E. Front, State St., Mill, the W.J.&S. railroad and Lake Elmer (A. Bolnick saw and grist mill). One part.

sheet-2.description: The northern end of Elmer as drawn in 1924, a residential district of the borough north and west of the business centre. The sheet is bounded at the top by North Main Street, with a single row of lots on its north side, and at the bottom by Chestnut Street, which crosses the lower part of the sheet on a diagonal. Between them run three parallel cross streets, 4th Street on the left, 3rd Street in the middle and 2nd Street along the right edge, cut halfway down by Oak Street, which ends at the diagonal of Chestnut Street. Most of the area is laid out in deep house lots with frame dwellings, many with small sheds, coops and auto garages behind them. The north side of North Main Street carries an auto storage and show room, a repair shop, a concrete-block building marked vacant, and near the right edge a lumber and storage yard with a 600-gallon water tank on a 30 ft elevation and a gasoline engine. A carpenter shop with a gasoline engine stands within the block between 3rd and 2nd Streets. West of 4th Street the large block numbered 101 is almost empty, with one dwelling. The lower block, numbered 102, is likewise thinly built. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are shown along the streets, with hydrants at several corners, and the streets are lettered 50 ft wide. Blocks are numbered 53 to 57 and 101 to 102. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper left; the sides marked no exposure have nothing beyond them on this sheet, and the right edge is continued on sheet 3.
notes: Right edge continues on sheet 3 (marked 3 at 2nd Street).
Map (50 ft). N. Main, 4th, 3rd, 2nd Streets, Oak, Chestnut; residential north end. Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: The north-west part of Elmer's business district in 1924 and the residential streets above it. North Main Street runs down the right half of the sheet from the top edge to East Front Street and on to State Street and Mill Street at the bottom right; 2nd Street runs along the top, Oak Street comes in at the upper left, and Chestnut Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to West Front Street. West Front Street and East Front Street cross the sheet below the middle. The upper part is residential, with frame dwellings on 2nd Street and along both sides of Chestnut Street and North Main Street (numbered about 116 to 199), and in block 57 a windmill with a 2,000-gallon water tank elevated 25 ft, a silo, barns and an ice house. Around the Front Street junction stand the First Presbyterian Church, a tile garage for 30 cars and a concrete-block garage for 20 cars. South of Front Street, between Front and State Streets, the sheet is the commercial core: stores along North Main Street, hardware and paint stores, a tin shop, lumber storage, the Elmer Times printing office, a fire house with a hand engine and hook and ladder truck, and the Frank Sturr saw mill and lumber yard with its lumber shed. The Elmer Branch and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad cross the bottom right corner near Mill Street. The lower left corner is cut off by a heavy line enclosing an inset of an outlying factory, which is not part of this map. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: West Front and East Front are today's Front Street.
First Presbyterian Church, the Elmer Times printing office, a fire house and the Frank Sturr saw mill and lumber yard are on this part.
Chestnut / Front was not used: OpenStreetMap has two Chestnut / Front nodes 34 m apart and the drawn junction lies between them.

Map (50 ft). Two parts: 1 main map (2nd St, Oak, Chestnut, N. Main, W./E. Front, State, Mill St; business district); 2 inset at lower left, Robert K. Greenwood Spindle Mfg. on Palatine Rd., 'located 2 miles S. of P.O.' (not placed).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Robert K. Greenwood Spindle Mfg., Palatine Rd., located 2 miles S. of P.O. (junction identity uncertain: the likeliest, Palatine Road / Lower Mill Road / Griers Lane (39.5534, -75.1810), is 2.9 miles from the post office and the drawn road leaves Palatine Road about 20 degrees off the modern Lower Mill Road; no mill pond near it in OpenStreetMap; needs identification of the mill site (Palatine Road, Upper Pittsgrove), then one hand-picked point with px_per_ft 7.75 and north_deg about 37).

sheet-4.description: The centre of Elmer in 1924, on both sides of South Main Street from Mill Street at the top of the sheet to Centre Street at the bottom, with Church Street leading east off South Main Street and Broad Street coming in from the south-west across the railroad. The upper left quarter is taken up by the railroad: the Pennsylvania Railroad's West Jersey and Seashore line runs diagonally across the sheet, with the Elmer Branch curving off to the north-west, a freight station with its platform, a freight shed, a passenger station, a warehouse for paints and hardware, a tool house, and a 50,000-gallon water tank with a pump house and well beside the track. The business frontage on South Main Street between Mill and Church Streets holds stores, a pool room, a hall above a drug store, the post office, the First National Bank and a town hall marker, and the M.E. Church with its tower stands on the east side north of Church Street. Further south along South Main Street are the Elmer High School, an undertaker's, a bakery with an oven, a moving picture theatre and a long row of frame dwellings with numbered house fronts from about 100 to 169. Much of the west half of the sheet below Broad Street is drawn as open ground, with a few coops near Centre Street. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches run along the streets. Streets are lettered 40 to 60 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with north towards the upper right; the area east of the block fronting South Main Street is marked no exposure.
notes: Centre is today's Center Street.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) and its Elmer Branch are abandoned; no running line remains in OpenStreetMap.
Joins sheet 1 at Mill Street, sheet 3 to the north-west, sheet 5 at Centre Street, sheets 6 and 8 to the west.
Map (50 ft). S. Main from Mill to Centre, Church, Broad; railroad stations, M.E. Church, Elmer High School. One part.

sheet-5.description: The south end of Elmer's main street in 1924, covering South Main Street from Centre Street at the top of the sheet down past Park Avenue to its junction with Salem Street, with Barton Avenue running south from Salem Street near the bottom left. The east edge of the sheet is the shore of Lake Elmer and the creek below its dam. The frontage on both sides of South Main Street is lined with frame dwellings, numbered from about 200 to 327, with sheds, coops and wood sheds behind them; near the lake there is a wood-working shop with paint storage, a blacksmith and a repository, and ice houses on the shore. At the foot of the street, where Salem Street comes in, stand the Elmer Lake Hotel and, beside the creek, the C. H. Ward grist mill (capacity 50 barrels daily, steam and water power) and the C. H. Oliphant creamery and ice cream manufactory. A machine shop stands on Centre Street near the top. The western half of the sheet, between Park Avenue and Salem Street and in block 65 below Salem Street, is largely open ground with a few dwellings. Water pipes of four and six inches run along the streets. Streets are lettered 30 to 60 ft wide; Barton Avenue is 30 ft. Blocks are numbered 10 to 14 and 65. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; the west side is marked no exposure, and the sheet joins sheet 4 at Centre Street and sheet 6 to the west.
notes: Centre is today's Center Street; Barton is Barton Avenue.
Salem Street meets South Main Street in a wide open junction at the grist mill; the junction and Barton / Salem were hand-picked (the detector paired a lot line on the 30 ft Barton).
Map (50 ft). S. Main from Centre to Salem, Park Av., Barton; Lake Elmer, C.H. Ward grist mill, C.H. Oliphant creamery. One part.

sheet-6.description: The district south of Broad Street between Elmer Street and the mill stream, in Elmer in 1924. Broad Street runs along the top of the sheet, with the end of Penn Street lettered on its north side; Elmer Street forms the left edge, and Cottage (Penn) runs south from Broad Street to the railroad siding. Centre Street crosses the lower half of the sheet on a diagonal and Park Avenue the bottom left corner, both starting from the junction with Elmer Street at the left edge. A stream, apparently the outlet of Lake Elmer's tributary, flows down from Broad Street across the sheet to the south-west, and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad crosses it diagonally, with a railroad siding running east from Elmer Street. Along Broad Street stands a row of frame dwellings and stores, numbered 104 to 132, with a windmill-fed water tank behind them. East of Cottage are a garage for 20 cars, greenhouses, grain storage, the Elmer Creamery (I. B. Reeve, proprietor) with an ice house, a shirt factory with storage and a warehouse and manufacturing room, and a gas machine. Industry lines the railroad: E. Bostwick's concrete block manufacturing works with a lime house and cement warehouse, warehouses, the Standard Oil Co. tanks, and at the lower left the large Garden State Canning Factory with its process room, soldering and can-making rooms, box shop, warehouses and packing room. The area south of Centre Street is open ground with only a few dwellings. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right.
notes: Cottage (Penn) is today's Cottage Avenue; Centre is Center Street.
Garden State Canning Factory, E. Bostwick's concrete block works, Elmer Creamery and a shirt factory on this sheet.

Along Broad Street the sheet draws Elmer Street to Cottage 575 ft apart against 528 ft between the modern junctions, about 8 percent more; the part is fitted through three points (an exact fit) and is low confidence.
Map (50 ft). Broad, Elmer, Cottage (Penn), Centre, Park Av.; Garden State Canning Factory, Elmer Creamery, shirt factory. One part; Broad drawn about 8 percent long between Elmer and Cottage.

sheet-7.description: The western residential district of Elmer in 1924, south of Broad Street between Union Street and Elmer Street. Broad Street runs along the top of the sheet with a continuous row of frame dwellings on its south side, numbered 202 to 232 east of Union Street and 300 to 318 west of it, among them a bakery with its oven and bake house, a carpet weaving shop and a hardware and tin shop. Union Street runs down from Broad Street, crosses Centre Street and bends south-west towards Salem Street, which crosses the lower left part of the sheet. Centre Street runs diagonally from Union Street to Elmer Street at the right edge, with houses numbered 211 to 242 along it. Elmer Street forms the right edge of the sheet, with dwellings numbered 115 to 137 and an office on its west side. The large block numbered 11 below Centre Street is mostly open; in its lower right corner the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses on a diagonal, with a siding serving the Elmer Lumber Co. yard: lumber sheds, lumber piles, a warehouse for building material, a paint store and an office. Blocks are numbered 8, 9, 11, 51, 52 and 65. Water pipes of four and six inches are shown, and streets are lettered 40 to 60 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; it joins sheet 8 across Broad Street, sheet 6 across Elmer Street and sheet 9 to the west.
notes: Centre is today's Center Street.
Elmer Lumber Co. yard on the railroad at the lower right.
Salem / Union was left out of the fit: the detected junction lies about 12 m east of the modern node, and the 1924 junction is drawn as a wide meeting of several roads.
Map (50 ft). Broad, Union, Centre, Elmer, Salem; Elmer Lumber Co. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: The lower half of sheet 8 of the 1924 Elmer atlas, below the heavy line that divides the sheet: the blocks between State Street and Broad Street from Elmer Street on the left to the stream called Small Run and beyond on the right, with Penn Street crossing them and the top of Cottage Street lettered below Broad Street. Block 60, north of State Street, holds a few dwellings and a carpenter shop; block 58, between Elmer and Penn Streets, has dwellings on its corners and the R.C. Church on Broad Street; block 59, east of Penn Street, contains a large concrete-block garage for 50 cars with a show room facing Broad Street. Small Run flows south across the sheet under State and Broad Streets, and beside it stand the pump house and stand pipe of The Elmer Water Co. and the Boro Hall with the fire department. Water pipes of six, eight and ten inches are shown in the streets, with hydrants. Streets are lettered 50 and 60 ft wide. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; the right half of block 2 is largely vacant.
notes: Cottage St. is today's Cottage Avenue.
Boro Hall and fire department, The Elmer Water Co. pump house and stand pipe, and the R.C. Church are on this part.
Broad / Cottage was hand-picked; the street is drawn only as far as the sheet edge.

Map (50 ft). Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower half (Elmer, Penn, State, Broad, Cottage St.; Boro Hall, Elmer Water Co., R.C. Church); 2 upper half (State, Daws = today's Union Street north of Broad, Broad, Elmer; First Baptist Church).

sheet-8-2.description: The upper half of sheet 8 of the 1924 Elmer atlas, above the heavy line that divides the sheet: the blocks between State Street and Broad Street west of Elmer Street, with Daws Street crossing them. Block 61, north of State Street, is mostly open, with a few dwellings and outbuildings near Elmer Street. Block 50, between State and Broad Streets east of Daws Street, is lined with frame dwellings numbered 206 to 230 on State Street and 201 to 229 on Broad Street, and holds the First Baptist Church with its tower on Broad Street. Block 62, west of Daws Street, has a few dwellings and a concrete-block auto house on Broad Street. Water pipes of six and eight inches run along State and Elmer Streets. Streets are lettered 40 ft (Daws) and 60 ft (State, Broad) wide. Broad Street is drawn only to its north edge here; its south side is on sheet 7. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; the area north of State Street at the top is marked no exposure.
notes: Daws is today's Union Street (Salem County 662) north of Broad Street; it met Broad Street about 15 m west of Union Street's line south of Broad, an offset the modern road no longer has, so Broad / Union was not used.
First Baptist Church on Broad Street.

Map (50 ft). Two parts split by a heavy line: 1 lower half (Elmer, Penn, State, Broad, Cottage St.; Boro Hall, Elmer Water Co., R.C. Church); 2 upper half (State, Daws = today's Union Street north of Broad, Broad, Elmer; First Baptist Church).

sheet-9-1.description: The western edge of Elmer in 1924, along Broad Street west of Union Street. Broad Street runs across the top of the sheet; a street lettered (Centre) runs south from it to Centre Street, which comes in from the right, and continues south-west as Hitchner Street to Salem Street, which crosses the lower part of the sheet on a diagonal. The north side of Broad Street, in block 62 (50), has a short row of frame dwellings numbered 323 to 337 near the right edge and a barn and outbuildings further west; the south side, in block 52, has dwellings numbered 322 to 345 and School No. 2, a two-storey building heated by stoves with two fire extinguishers. Centre Street has dwellings numbered 330 to 345 on both sides, and block 51 between Centre, Hitchner and Salem Streets holds a few dwellings and outbuildings on deep lots, numbered about 309 to 331 on Salem Street. West of Hitchner Street the large block 63 (51) and the land along Broad Street are drawn as vacant. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B crosses Broad Street at the left, joining the strip drawn below the heavy line at the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of four and six inches run along the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; it joins sheet 7 at the right and sheet 8 across Broad Street.
notes: The street lettered (Centre) between Broad Street and Centre Street is today the north end of Hitchner Avenue.
School No. 2 on Broad Street.

Placed from Broad / Hitchner, a hand-picked Hitchner / Salem and two seam points carried from sheet 7; Centre / Hitchner, hand-picked, was left out (6 m residual, the drawn bend of Hitchner at Centre does not match the modern node). Medium-low confidence.

Map (50 ft). Two parts: 1 main map (Broad, (Centre) = north end of Hitchner Avenue, Centre, Hitchner, Salem; School No. 2); 2 strip below a heavy line continuing Broad St west to Salem St (A-B match line).

sheet-9-2.description: A narrow strip at the foot of sheet 9 of the 1924 Elmer atlas, below a heavy line, continuing Broad Street westward from the A-B match line on the main part of the sheet to the edge of the borough where Salem Street branches off to the south-west at the lower left corner. Broad Street runs straight across the strip; its north side, in block 62 (50), has one frame dwelling and two outbuildings near the left end, and its south side, block 63 (51), is marked no exposure. A hydrant at the left end carries the note 65 ft beyond, and a four-inch water pipe runs along Broad Street. Broad Street is lettered 60 ft wide and Salem Street 50 ft. The strip is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main part of the sheet, 50 ft to an inch with north towards the upper right; the open area above the heavy line at the left belongs to block 64.
notes: Placed from one point carried from part 1 (Broad Street at the A-B match line) at the atlas scale and part 1's rotation; the modern Broad / Salem junction lies about 18 m beyond where this places the drawn one. Low confidence.

Map (50 ft). Two parts: 1 main map (Broad, (Centre) = north end of Hitchner Avenue, Centre, Hitchner, Salem; School No. 2); 2 strip below a heavy line continuing Broad St west to Salem St (A-B match line).
